summary: The pain is real, but GitHub's native stacked PRs and the coding agents are absorbing it, and four free splitters already exist. File-level LLM splitting also tends to break builds, and there is no evidence anyone would pay.

demand.evidence: Evidence covers the problem (review complaints 3.8% to 4.8%, dev.to; GitHub blog on agent-decomposed stacks) but nothing shows anyone wants or would pay for a separate tool. Four free competitors already listed in RESEARCH.md.

statusQuo.evidence: Manual git add -p / rebase, or simply asking Claude Code/Cursor to split the branch. Cheap and improving; the tool's validation loop is the only edge.

specificity.evidence: PRD names only categories (individual developers, teams, maintainers). No named person, role or consequence.

wedge.evidence: A read-only split plan is what Tessl and a plain prompt already do. The valuable version (build-verified, hunk-level) is hard and the PRD excludes hunk-level splitting.

futureFit.evidence: Platform-native stacks and agents that decompose their own work make a standalone splitter less essential over three years.

premises: Large PRs are a painful bottleneck: supported by dev.to data and the GitHub blog.
A separate tool is the right fix: not supported; GitHub and agents are absorbing it and free tools exist.
LLM file-level grouping yields independently buildable PRs: doubtful, cross-file dependencies are an open question in the PRD.
Developers will let a tool create branches and PRs automatically: unverified.
A solo CLI has a path to revenue: no evidence.
alternatives: Minimal: a Claude Code skill/prompt that proposes a split and runs validation (Tessl already does this).
Extend David's PR Receipt idea (ideas/pr-receipt) with a PR-size signal; nearer-term measurable pain.
Ideal: hunk-level, build-verified stacking engine as a GitHub App; large effort and exposed to GitHub's roadmap.
Lateral: a PR-size-gate GitHub Action that comments a suggested split plan.
wedge: A read-only GitHub Action that comments a suggested split plan on PRs over N files; still undifferentiated from free alternatives.

feasibility.notes: Node/TypeScript CLI with local Ollama is buildable in a weekend, but a hosted LLM-backed service is not $0 and a free local CLI has no revenue path. The one test: on three real 20+ file branches, each proposed group builds and passes tests in order; expected to fail on at least one.

risks: Platform absorption: GitHub native stacked PRs and agent-built decomposition
File-level splits break builds; dependency detection needs per-language analysis
Four free incumbents and no price point for a solo CLI
Trust barrier for tools that rewrite branches and open PRs
No path from free CLI to revenue
killCriteria: Drop if: fewer than 5 of 50 visitors sign up in two weeks; the build-verified test fails on 2 of 3 real branches; GitHub or Claude Code ships agent-driven splitting covering the use case; or nobody names a team that would pay.
